Note that log cutting does this conversion automatically when the trees are depleted, but not all terrain can be logged.

If it is not eligible you are told as much, and would have to make it suitable for conversion by removing everything that isn't grass or soil.  Mining zones are useful to remove pavement, for instance.  Note that removal of buildings is dangerous, laborious, and may still fail to get rid of everything if e.g. a basement or an opening to underground areas (such as a manhole) remains.

"I don't have long before I die - and before I do, I have to say something important, something you MUST remember."  She looks back at the camera with a pained half-smile and gritted teeth, speaking with a low but sincere tone.  "You, you watching this video, don't ever give up, keep pushing, don't call it quits by killing yourself.  Keep going for as long as you can."  Her voice trembles and her eyes get watery, "I… believe there are people out there in this hell, people like you, who can make things better."  The woman is trying her best to hold back the agonized tears streaming down her disheveled face as her voice starts to crack.  "Find happiness and friends wherever you can, and remember you've got a purpose, and that purpose is not only to survive, it's to thrive."  She lets out an anguished gasp, nearly doubling over in pain before stammering out "Promise me, please, j-just promise me whoever you are, that you'll do that, please."  She then tries to grab the phone off the table to stop recording, but it falls onto the floor the video doesn't end until 7 seconds later.  In the time remaining, she languorously picks the phone off the floor and holds it close to her face - it is only then you register just how bloodshot her eyes are.

"It's always a different dream, but always kind of the same.  I stand in a hallway and knock on a door for a joke, but I can't turn and run when the doorknob starts turning.  I stand up mockingly in class while the teacher's back is turned, but can't seem to sit back down as they turn back to look at me.   I dive into the beautiful, clear ocean, but freeze in place just below the surface as something rises from below to meet me."

"Do you feel any guilt about the work you do here, Jason?"

"You know I'm not allowed to talk about any specifics."

"Of course, but I haven't asked what you're doing, I asked how you feel about it."

"I don't feel like we're doing anything wrong here.  On the contrary, I think leaving the work undone would be a thing to feel guilty about.  The untapped potential, the understanding we're building… it will change how we think of the world.  That has to be a good thing, right?"

"And yet, in your dreams you feel like a kid caught with their hands in the cookie jar."

"I'd rather we drop this line of discussion, Doctor."

"Naturally, Jason.  Or would "Chief Investigator" make you feel more in control?"

"We are seen.  It's not long until we will be touched."

"Touched by what, exactly?"

"Touched.  Chewed.  Tasted.  Digested.  Processed.  Excreted."

"Ramin, focus, please.  What is doing all that?  Or rather, what do you feel will be doing those things?"

"It's big.  Bigger than the Sun.  Smaller than an atom."

"And what does this large small thing want, beyond touching us?"

"It just is.  It needs no reason.  It needs only to exist.  It needs only to expand."

"Do you want to talk about Immersion 132R?"

"There's nothing to talk about.  I wasn't there.  It didn't touch me.  I didn't look.  It didn't look back.  It didn't smile with a million rotten worlds in its mouth."

"Have you been taking your medication?"

"Like they would help.  I tried, Doc, I really did.  But the truth is, I like having these thoughts.  They give me a certainty, and I am thankful for knowing how it will all end.  That we all belong to something, and nothing can take us from it now."

"Please state your name and ID for the record."

"Dr. Maria Catarina Gonzales, S-7531."

"Thank you, Doctor.  You know why we're here, don't you?  Please tell us about your previous project supervisor."

"Ruslan was…"

"Ruslan?"

"I'm sorry, Dr. Lavochkin was extremely enthusiastic about our research when I arrived in the facility.  That enthusiasm had a way of dragging people with him, you know?  We wanted to see our subjects as he did, full of wonder and untapped potential."

"Did he ever tell you what it was that you were working on?"

"Not really, no.  We were to "characterize the effects of need-to-knowium on a wide range of living subjects" was his little joke, back when he made jokes."

"When did that change?"

"He became a lot more distant when we began testing PE050 and PE150, the intravenous formulation.  He sent us back to the pods way before he left the lab, and he started muttering about "preparing the world" for something under his breath.  That coincided with him requisitioning more… exotic test subjects."

"How did he rationalize those?"

"He could be very convincing, and we were happy to see that spark again.  You want to hear about the centipedes, right?  L.coeculus are parthenogenetic and completely lack social behavior, making them a reasonable long-term subjects for PE050's "societal predisposition" effects, as we liked to call it."

"Do you still consider that decision "reasonable"?"

"Not in the light of what happened, I suppose.  But your people kicking in the observation room's door and starting shooting wasn't the most reasonable course of action either, if we're being honest."

"We're not here to review the actions of Security on that day.  Did he ever mention anywhere he could be hiding?"

"We weren't close, so no he didn't share the location of his secret treehouse.  With those things in tow he shouldn't be too hard to find though -- just follow the song of the centipedes."

"Thank you for the advice, Doctor.  I am to inform you that you are restricted to your residential pod until the review of your involvement in the incident is concluded.  You are expected to finish any remaining reports in the meantime, but your workstation will be isolated from the facility network otherwise."

"Please state your name for the record."

"Fuck off."

"You are in possession of a fake driver's license issued to one Jonathan Smith, which is the alias you applied for employment with in our facility.  We will find out your real name in time, but I'll refer to you as Mr. Smith for this interview.  Is that acceptable, Mr. Smith?"

"Fuck off.  I want to talk to my lawyer."

"You don't have a lawyer."

"I know my rights, shithead.  You won't get a word out of me before I talk to my lawyer."

"You seem to be confused about your situation, Mr. Smith.  As far as the world is concerned you stopped existing the moment you entered this facility, and as far as we are concerned you stopped having rights as soon as you tried to access areas above your provisional clearance.  Let me present your options going forward:  You continue withholding information from us and you will suffer a meticulously-documented accident leaving no doubt to your demise even though no body will ever be found.  Or you cooperate fully and without hesitation, in which case you will get to see the sky again and act like nothing has happened.  Am I understood?"

"…yes."

"Please state your name for the record."

"M-my name is Thomas Wright.  I'm a, uh, a freelance journalist."

"What were you trying to accomplish in this facility, Mr. Wright?"

"There was th-this guy offering good money for some pictures from the inside of this place."

"I don't suppose this man told you his name?"

"No, no… He just handed me the application forms and the license, paid quarter up front, and said to bring the pictures to the same spot in a week's time."

"What did he say to expect here?"

"This place is… look, you can't expect people not to talk about it, right?  You can't just put up a warehouse of a shipping company nobody's heard of practically overnight and act like it was always here.  He said you guys were a, uh, top secret prison for political prisoners."

"That explains your attempts to clumsily pick the first closed door you came across.  How did your employer contact you?"

"A friend of a friend gave him my number, at least according to him.  If you haven't noticed in here times are tough, so I couldn't really afford to be picky about work even before he started throwing cash around."

"Very well.  While we verify that account my colleagues here will take you through a tour of our facility:  You will take photographs with your "hidden" camera when and where they instruct you to.  You will submit these pictures for review and remain in our custody until we can be certain of your compliance.  You will be released and at the appointed time you will hand over the pictures to your employer.  You will not mention this conversation to them, or to anybody outside of this room.  You will enjoy your well-earned payment, far away from this facility.  Am I understood?"

"Yes, sir, I can do that."

"Excellent, Mr. Wright.  I look forward to never seeing you again."

Select option <color_light_cyan>Wait until you catch your breath</color> to fully restore all lost stamina.

Be careful about doing too many strenuous activities as you will build up your weariness over time, which will stack movement and action penalties on top of your stamina cost.  You can watch your <color_light_cyan>Weary Transition</color> in the sidebar as you are performing longer activities to see their effect on your weariness. I was especially good at enforcing the law, had a special yellow pistol I called ole blue that showed how far I'd come from when I started with a blue pistol I called ole yellow.  By all rights I should be dead.  We were called to control "riots", which we all know were the first <zombie> hordes.  Fat lot of good we were.  Pretty sure we killed more civilians.  Even among my crew, morale was piss poor and we were shooting wild.  Then something hit us, something big.  Might have been a bomb, I really don't remember.  I woke up pinned underneath a lot of bodies.  I couldn't see anything… but I could hear it.  <swear!>.  I could hear everything.  I spent hours, maybe days under those bodies, not even trying to get out.

Eventually yes.  It had been quiet for hours.  I was parched, injured, and terrified.  My training was maybe the only thing that kept me from freaking out.  I decided to try to pull myself out and see how bad my injuries were.  It was quite easy.  The people on top of me were torn open, and it turned out I was basically just lying under a little debris, with parts of people tented around me.  I wasn't even too badly hurt.  I grabbed as much to eat as I could, and I slipped away.  It was night.  I could hear fighting farther away in the woods, so I went the other way.  I made it a while before I ran into any <zombies>… I ran from them.  I ran, and I ran, and I ran some more.  And here I am.

It was just <freaking> chaos out there, man.  But I'm used to chaos.  You don't live as long as I've lived and not know how to keep away from a fight you can't win.  Biggest worry wasn't the zombies and the monsters, honestly.  It was that something even worse was coming.

Kept outta their line of sight, is a big part of it.  Don't let those <freaking> flyin' eyeballs get you, you know?  I kept my head down until I got past the worst of it, but then one of the <freaking> flying eyeballs saw me and I had to book it.  I wound up on the edge of a river layin' low under a hollow tree for a few hours, then slipped away in the night.

Bullshit, that's what.  The assholes busted me on possession, wasn't even my fuckin' stash.  I don't do weed, man, that shit's nasty, I was just carryin' it for my buddy Johnny.  Y'know, this might be a <freaking> hellhole now, but if I've seen the last power-trippin' asshole pistol man, it might all be worth it.

I was fricking lucky for <the_cataclysm>.  I was squatting in a little canoe by the river.  I was in a real shitty place, and my crew had mostly just been arrested for trespassing, but I had skipped out.  I was scared they were gonna think I ratted 'em out and come get me, but hey, no worries about that now.

Yeah.  Giant dragonflies.  A bunch of them, some of them I'm pretty sure were fuckin', I shit you not.  I dunno what brought them way out my way but they saw me takin' a piss and that was that.  I took a few shots at them but they didn't stop, so I ran.  Once I got my shit together again I realized it wasn't so bad, I was running out of stuff anyway.  Been livin' on what I can grab ever since, until I fell in with you.
I made it to one of those <freaking> caves, but it was almost worse than what I left behind.  Escaped from there, been on the run since.

Same as most people who didn't get killed straight up during the riots.  I went to one of those stupid <freaking> cave death traps.  I actually lived there for a while with three others.  One guy who I guess had a lot of good mojo kinda ran the show, because he seemed to really know what was going on.  Spoiler alert: he fucking didn't.

Well, I assume you know about the riots and the freakin' nightmare monsters walking the earth beside zombies, right?  If you're asking what I think caused it all, well, I dunno.  My best guess it was some huge overreach, maybe some kind of experimental weapon that got away.  They tried to lie so much at the start about everything that was going on, I don't think any of it measures up.  They were trying to cover something up.  As for the real end times, maybe the rest of the world tried to contain it.  I heard about all kinds of wild stuff.  To me that seems like somewhere else trying to get whatever is going on here contained.  Maybe it even worked.  It's bad now but it's not like it was.

How could you not know what happened?  The world damn well ended, that's what.  And it didn't start with an earthquake, birds, snakes, or music.  It started with riots, and they had to dispatch violent goons to take care of the <freaking> criminals.  The leadership tried to pad it claiming it was some kind of mind control, but I didn't see too much different from the usual bullshit: entitled babies looking for an excuse to break the law.  It just got way worse, this time, until it was time to get away.  I heard rumors they were even burning some places to try to control it - which, I have to admit, is maybe a bit too hard-core.

She was alone when the fires started and the world went to hell.  I was working on something.  I tried to make it to her, but the whole area was a war zone.  Things I can't describe lurching along, crushing people and worse.  Some people were trying to stop them, but hitting other people trying to get away as much as anything.  And then the collateral damage would get right back up and join the enemy.  If it hadn't been for my wife, I would have just left, but I did what I could and I slipped through.  I actually <freaking> made it alive.

To be honest… I don't really remember.  I remember vague details of my life before the world was like this, but <the_cataclysm> itself?  It's all a blur.  I don't know how I got where I am now, or how any of this happened.  I think something pretty bad must have happened to me.  Or maybe I was just hit in the head really hard.  Or both.  Both seems likely.  First thing I remember is seeing a beautiful young woman with her face covered with blood, laughing and saying everything had fallen and it was all over.

Who I was is gone.  All that stuff burned away in <the_cataclysm>.  Got it?  Who I am now started two days into it.  I was on the run from a big-ass hell zombie, running like I'd always been doing, when I found a stick laying on the ground.  I took it as a sign and beat that gooey bastard to a pulp… and that's when I became me.  I still run, because who doesn't, but I stand my ground now.

We got to my buddy's place, but the <freaking> spearmen had been there first.  It was all boarded up and there was a wooden barricade out front.  One of those <freaking> giant insects… <freaking> got Buck.  Almost got me too.  I managed to get my pup… get him outta there, that… it wasn't easy, had to use a dead bug as a shield.  And then, well, while I was still cryin', Buck came back.  I had to… <swear!>.  I… I can't say it.  You know.

LOCAL WIZARD DIES, INVESTIGATION CONTINUES

Investigations are continuing into the death of local wizard Sivi, daughter of Ḥalmet of Clan Redaxe, who was found dead in her home last month.  No foul play is suspected at this time.  An initial report by medical examiners at Massachusetts General Hospital indicated the cause of death as multiple organ failure following a sudden illness.  "It's very strange", said a source close to the matter, "Her organs all looked like those of an elderly person, even though 96 is barely middle-age for a dwarf.  She could have expected to live another hundred years easily.  If you ask me, it's all that research she was doing into the effects of Haste magic.  Probably hasted herself right through to the end of her life.  We've seen side effects in Haste over-usage before but never to a fatal degree."  When asked for comment, Dr. Olivia Wright, a professor of control thaumaturgy at MIT&M, said, "The idea of "haste-death" shows up in rumors repeatedly but there has never been a single confirmed case.  Haste places stress on the body, of course, but the stress is accounted for as part of the effects of the spell.  Ms. Sivi's death was tragic, but fearmongering about the effects of magic helps no one."

COPPER PRIME combat implications

A common question is, why does JUNIPER GOLD have a specific combat-focused division and COPPER PRIME does not?  There are two main reasons.

The first is that fire spreads.  The use of JUNIPER GOLD poses little extra risk unless an incautious mathematician causes structural damage sufficient to induce a collapse.  Any use of COPPER PRIME can start a fire, and the ability to extinguish fires is far from universal among COPPER PRIME mathematicians.

The second is the short range.  This is a consistent problem with all mathematics, but the danger of uncontrolled COPPER PRIME usage provides an extra disadvantage.

In essence, COPPER PRIME has many of the same disadvantages of flamethrowers that led to them no longer being used in active service without few advantages to counteract this; primarily a lack of fuel requirements.  Unless the range problem is solved, military applications of COPPER PRIME will always take a secondary role behind JUNIPER GOLD.

Let's start with the obvious.  Teleportation is moving faster than light, by definition.  Even though our most powerful mathematicians can currently only teleport a few grams a few meters distant, we've used slow-motion photography and confirmed that while the transit is not instantaneous, it's still faster than c.  So, as the saying goes, relativity, causality, faster than light travel, pick two, right?  Which are we going to pick?

Well, as much as it pains me as a physicist to say it, relativity, at least as it relates in this case.  Now we have a third domain alongside quantum mechanics and general relativity: Netherum mathematics.  While I hesitate to speculate on something that we have collected so little data on, it is possible that the Netherum provides its own reference frame coterminous with our own (or multiple) realities.  If we built our satellites with matrix technology, would they still need to account for time dilation?  Would relativity override Netherum mathematics in that case?

But to return to the title: there is no evidence time travel is possible despite repeated attempts.  Perhaps if we had a LOST RAIN mathematician capable of moving interstellar distances we could ask them to come back before they left.  Barring that, I'm afraid asking LOST RAIN to retroactively avert any disasters is not on the table.

The basic question is, are we better than the boys over in VERDANT HAND, and the answer is yes.  They're faster but we don't even need to cross the distance.  They hit harder but we build up twice the momentum in half the time.

You died in the Cataclysm.  Perhaps during the Cataclysm itself, perhaps in the riots leading up to it.  Someone killed you and hastily dumped you in a shallow grave, and that should have been the end.

But it wasn't.  Your rage at your own death, your thirst for vengeance, the sheer unfairness of it all, dragged you out of the grave and propelled you onward.  You can feel your murderer, out there in the world, and will stop at nothing until you've tracked them down.  You don't need to eat, sleep, or breathe anymore.  All you need is revenge.

To create a dream-drainer mosquito's heart, you'll need to gather some doses of lotus blossom, a handful of wyld candies, a small pile of dreamdross and a liter of Fae blood to create the dream-draining catalyst.

Once it is completed, find a mosquito and activate the catalyst while no farther than five meters away from it.  It must be a mosquito, anything else won't work.  The mosquito will then gorge itself on the catalyst and will suddenly transform into a dream-eating nightmare.

Once the dream-drainer mosquito appears, kill it and the heart will be yours.

Be careful, as this mosquito wields powers akin to those of the Eaters of Dreams such as the ability to heal its wounds and throw piercing projectiles at you.

But your limbs and other parts will be exchangeable, like bionics.  In the future, if you take off a limb, you'll have to remove your CBMs, fix them, clean them, and reinstall them.

Aye, so this one's a lot like mine.  Real popular among this Exodii node.  It's heavy duty, but as you can see, it's a little less human-like than maybe you're comfortable with.  It's a good, sturdy design, that will keep you safe.  But you'll have to get used to going without most clothing and armor.  The body just isn't made for them.  This is my suggestion.

This one's for the nostalgic, I suppose, like Venn here.  You'll still have a human shape, and can still do and wear all your human things.  Downside is it can't be plated as well, so it's a bit more vulnerable by itself.
No.  You'll be wearing an Exodii-suit, but nobody is Exodii until they jump with the Exodii, and that remains to be seen.
Yes, of course.  I'll go back to the shop.  Find me if you reconsider.

Yes, it's done.  Don't waste time thinking about what's different.  You're still there, just inside a tough steel case.  It won't be easy to adapt, but keep a stiff upper lip - or be brave - as you might say.  Try to keep everything intact, but if you get any damage, come back here.  Venn'll do repairs in exchange for materials.

Ahh, now that's a big question.  Not something I'd share with anyone who wandered in.  But yes, I know, you have one of our interfaces.  You carry our trust with you, and maybe you have the right to know.

Listen carefully:  not everything we gather comes from places like this.  Sometimes, we find places we call "labyrinths."  Stairs down to other worlds.  We keep track of them.  And, one is nearby, spotted by Benzete themselves.  These places aren't safe, and they aren't friendly.  But, they seem made for us, which is convenient, if you don't think too hard about it.  Honestly, it's where most of our bionics come from.

What are they, you ask?  If I knew, I'd be afraid to say.  They aren't like other places.  They don't just exist.  Something put them there, piece by piece.  A workshop of unknown purpose.  But also, not like any of that.  Honestly, not really sure if they exist before we pass by, or through them, anyway.  Anything we say about them is basically waxing religiously - maybe they can't be explained.

You find all manner of things.  But, you walk in and there are things where you might not expect them to be.  Tools ready to use.  Bionics ready to take, like bait on a snare, too tempting.  Listen carefully: you won't find gifts there.  You are a thief in the night, stealing what you want.  You're a fish, and the treasures are hooks.

No, not The Enemy, but something like their wife (Rubik is trying to be funny).  If you go, you'll see.  It'll talk to you.  It knows what shape to take, or it just takes it, anyway.  For me, an old friend, in a Temple of ale I barely remember.  For others, other things.  But, if it starts talking to you in a familiar way?  It it offers you safety?  Leave, quick and quiet.  It's a lie.  Death by another name.

Heh, just trying to be funny, when I shouldn't be.  A bad joke.  Nothing funny about it.  I meant only this: it isn't the Enemy the one that raises the dead here.  But, they're maybe similar in some way.  Not family, not part of the Enemy, but maybe an equal to it.  So don't take the joke for more than a joke.  It's not its partner, its wife, or its friend, because I doubt these things have such things.  Maybe just an illusion - a trick in the head.  But that's just my thinking - it's all unknown.

Getting there is tricky, but easier than moving a castle.  They're less expensive and dangerous than a whole jump, which itself is curious.  Downstairs is a metal ring with a terminal - I wrote the messages, so you'll understand it.  We'll consider you a volunteer who wants to scout the place out.  It's good for both of us.  You're free to use it.  Keep in mind that the teleporter needs to recharge for 5 days between jumps.  Your first time will leave you dizzy, but it'll pass if you're tough.

A word of caution: I can't tell you what you'll find.  They're always different.  Don't trust them.  Don't linger.  Use your head, think like an Exodii:  take what you can, but don't get tempted by treasure.

For me?  Well, twisted halls of steel.  But there's another place.  It's a little like a pub I barely remember, if it ever existed.  Warm.  Wood.  Fire.  Like a Temple (this should be capitalized, as it's what it calls itself for Rubik) for the soul, if I still have one.  But I don't stay there or trust it.  These days, I don't even visit.  I have other things to do, like run this shop.

killing for sport,
eating all the bodies--
actual cannibal Shia LaBeouf.
MAYA SACRIFICING GAMEPLAY FOR REALISM?  THE SHOCKING TRUTH REVEALED
The boomer tries to vomit more, but only droplets are thrown.

Getting the bodybag was harder than you would have thought, and ordinary garbage bags would just not do.  You eat your fill for the last time with this mouth, undress (you won't need clothes after the change), and climb in the bag.  Closing the zipper from the inside is a challenge, but you need complete darkness for what comes now.  You wait.
And wait.
And wait.

Could you have been wrong?  You were so sure the time was right.
You need to get out of here, but you can't move your…anything.  Do you even have anything to move?

You're a veteran of contests using just your fists.  Maybe you've even used your skills in fights against other tribes, if it came down to a contest of champions and both of you ended up without your weapons.
prof_desc_female

You've spent a chunk of your free time around the fire in camp or on boring moments out in the wild carving wood and bone into amusing or memorable shapes, and over time you've gotten pretty good at it.
prof_desc_female
Your people dwelt by the waters, and you were playing on and in them almost before you could walk.  You're familiar with both swimming and boating.
prof_desc_female

In your nomadic wanderings, your tribe relied on you to transport the larger goods like tents or baskets of preserved food and bedding, and you've gotten very good at packing efficiently and carrying goods for long distances, but you tend to have a pretty heavy tread when walking.
prof_desc_female

You passed your apprenticeship among the Wise, learning the lesser mysteries and undergoing the ordeal to bond your soul with that of the Forest.  You succeeded where many of your fellow apprentices failed and began to learn the deeper mysteries under the tutelage of your master.  Now you're on your own, but your knowledge will guide your way forward.
prof_desc_female

Tall tales of the ancients dominated your childhood as you squatted in the very ruins of what they had built.  Their lofty ideas of interstellar civilization never rang true as you fought the universe for every breath of air and bite of food.
prof_desc_female
You have plenty of practice at searching the forest for delicious foods.
prof_desc_female

While not usually one of the hunters, you've gone on hunts when food supplies were slow or some of the hunters were recovering from their injuries, and have developed skill with the bow because of it.
prof_desc_female
While not one of the warriors who went out on raids, you have fought in defense of your people and know how to handle yourself in a fight.
prof_desc_female
You have some experience driving land vehicles, and know how to operate them safely.
prof_desc_female

You helped dress and prepare the animals that came back from the hunt, and sometimes accompanied the hunters into the field if they were expecting a particularly large catch.  You're very good at preparing a carcass for food.
prof_desc_female

You spent long hours wandering far afield, looking for new hunting grounds, making sure the things of the forest and the swamps stayed away from your people's lands.  You are very good at spotting threats from far away, but you've grown used to spending time alone.
prof_desc_female
You were exiled from your tribe.  Whether you deserved it or not, it has forced you become self-reliant and stay on the move lest you meet others who know of your sentence.
prof_desc_female

You frequently took a turn with the basketweavers, staying awake as long as the fire gave enough light to provide the containers your people used to transport their food and possessions on their wanderings.  To this day you still don't need as much sleep as others do.
prof_desc_female

You were born attuned to the spirit world.  Normally that would have marked you out for apprenticeship to a shaman or one of the Wise, but for whatever reason, that did not happen.  Your unique senses have left you with some knowledge of the unseen world, as well as difficulty falling asleep.
prof_desc_female

Unlike most of your people, you always stayed up long past sunset, staring at the moon or walking at the edge of the firelight.  You are much better at seeing at night, but have a harder time falling asleep and waking up.
prof_desc_female
You served your people as a stonecarver, making the tools and weapons they needed to survive in the hostile wilderness.
prof_desc_female
You loved creating small dolls, toys, and bits of art during your downtime.  Now, you might want to channel those skills into making more practical things.
prof_desc_female
What survives from the past has proved its worth.  A new thing is risky--who knows if it will stand the test of time?  You cannot use modern technology.
prof_desc_female
Some people say marijuana isn't addictive.  For reasons you can no longer recall, you decided to prove them wrong.
prof_desc_female
You made your living running messages between the villages and tribes of the land, always priding yourself on being the fastest.  That speed is definitely going to help you now.
prof_desc_female

You were part of a squadron of skyfarers, plying the vastness to protect trade routes from nefarious air pirates.  Now you're adrift and alone, one vessel against an alien world swarming with the undead…
prof_desc_female
You are born anew, freshly spun forth from the natural elements but hours ago.  You have as yet had no time to develop hobbies.
prof_desc_female
For years you went out from your tribe's village, taking game and bringing it back to keep them fed.  Now that you're on your own, those skills will have to be enough to keep you alive.
prof_desc_female

You used to travel far beyond the safety of your people's lands.  Maybe you were a trader seeking new goods, or maybe you ranged far afield seeking new game, or maybe you just needed some time away from everyone else.  At least now you'll get some time alone.
prof_desc_female

Whether due to circumstances forcing ingenuity or just an unhealthy fascination with tinkering you're a certified MacGyver with a very wide range of fabrication knowledge.  You could probably make a functioning cannon out of a paper clip and some bubble gum.
prof_desc_female
You loved meeting new people during tribal gatherings, dancing around the fire until the late hours.  Maybe you can keep putting those skills to use.
prof_desc_female
All adults have to walk long hours and do physical labor to support their people.  You were no exception, leaving you well-conditioned to survive on your own.
prof_desc_female

You are one of the Scaled Ones, called "lizardfolk" by the warmbloods.  You keep mostly to yourselves in the swamps, hunting and fishing as you've always done, but something is happening in the world now and you've left your tribe to find out just what it is.
prof_desc_female
You used to accompany the hunters but not to flush out or chase the quarry.  Your task was to place snares in the path, so the others would harry your prey and your traps could catch them.
prof_desc_female
You know how to survive within interstellar civilization, know basic safety protocols, and there's little chance of you ever opening an airlock by mistake.
prof_desc_female

From your birth, you were in contact with the spirit world.  You were trained in the ways of the spirits and mediated between them and your tribe.  In time, one of the Wise came to your village to induct you into the deeper mysteries, but they vanished before completing your training.  Now that you're alone, you'll need to contact the spirits of this new place and learn their ways.
prof_desc_female
You were born a perfectly engineered bodyguard, grown in a corporate blacksite and given nothing to live for but your client.  That arrangement, however did not last.

You were an apprentice stonecarver, set to accomplish simple tasks like knife-knapping and finding flaking stones in the wild.
prof_desc_female
You once led a crew of skyfarers, traveling the skies for fame, bricks and sand.  Now you are on your own, and the ground is swarming with zombies.  At least this world has ground…

From your first hunt, you showed talent with a bow.  While the tribe was well guarded by your aim, you're all alone now.
prof_desc_female
You didn't hunt, and you didn't cook food, but your skills at brewing alcohol ensured that you were always valued at any tribal gathering larger than two or three people.
prof_desc_female
You used to tend the cookfires and prepare the meals, making sure that the meat didn't burn and the flames stayed hot until every one of your people was fed.
prof_desc_female
The land was your kin's long before the warmbloods came.  Someday, it will be yours again.
prof_desc_female
You're a lone skyfarer, scouting the endless blue for new routes across the sky.  Now you've caught sight of more land than you've seen in a lifetime, an unfamiliar land of monsters…
prof_desc_female

Your people may have used pipeleaf for ritual purposes but you were always a bit too…enthusiastic when your partook.  You'll need to find a steady supply of leaf to smoke if you want to keep the cravings at bay.
prof_desc_female

One among billions of the disenfranchised, you enlisted into UICA expeditionary forces to escape the oppressive poverty of Earth's metroplexes.  This only lead to your ignominious dismissal and abandonment in the frontier when the reclamation sputtered out without victory or glory.  You have roamed the frontier ever since, as a low-rate mercenary, scavenger and pirate.
prof_desc_female

Since you were young you were taught which plants to avoid and which ones can feed you in an emergency, how to follow water to the source, when fruits are in season, and to *never* stay out in the forest after dark.
prof_desc_female

You were born and raised within a corporate creche, were your every action was monitored to asses your value.  Once it became clear that you had no exceptional talents, you were cast out into the unemployable mass to fend for yourself.
prof_desc_female
Touring the frontier in search of intelligence and sabotage contracts may not be the most glamorous mercenary work, but pays well and keeps you out of the backstabbing in the corporate core.
prof_desc_female
You used to do backflips and splits to impress other members of your tribe, and you've maintained your flexibility.
prof_desc_female
You've spent enough time around the communal campfires that you know how to cook basic dishes and feed yourself.

Like most people within interstellar society, you have previously received cybernetic enhancement to make life easier.  Your enhancements include a universal data link, some basic power storage, and a charging cable to top up.

You used to climb trees and jump from branch to branch to impress the other youths in your tribe, and hours of jumping over stones and running down gully walls have paid off.  You'll be a great position to escape the next time you get into trouble.

You've got training and some experience in dealing with urgent injuries.  Away from your people, that'll have to do.

You've spent time fighting with your bare hands.  Not to take down game or against other tribes, of course, but in friendly--or at least, non-lethal--contests around the campfires.  You've gotten pretty good at it.

You remember the great luxury of your childhood, the endless parties underneath diamond-glass domes, the great entourages of servants and companions, and the backdoor plays and plots against your peers for the future of humanity. prof_desc_female
You are dead, but you are still moving, and there is someone out there who will be very unpleasantly surprised when they learn that.

You have a bit too much of a taste for the beverages served during tribal celebrations, but you've gotten used to fighting while under their spell.  Some of your fellows even say you fight better after you've had a few.
